tests.description: An aligned pair should get a straight line, not a degenerate dog-leg with zero-length segments.
tests.key: connectorPath › drops straight down when parent and child share a centre

tests.description: Siblings share that bus, which is what makes the tree read as one structure rather than a set of unrelated lines.
tests.key: connectorPath › routes through a horizontal bus midway between the two levels

tests.description: A connector that started inside the parent pill or stopped short of the child would leave visible gaps against the dotted stroke.
tests.key: connectorPath › starts at the parent bottom edge and ends at the child top edge

tests.description: A refusal is thrown by the caller, so nothing should be queued for a request that will never be sent.
tests.key: followUpMessages › appends nothing for a refusal

tests.description: An empty array is how the loop learns it is finished.
tests.key: followUpMessages › appends nothing when the turn is done

tests.description: The API requires the tool_results in a single user message following the assistant turn that requested them.
tests.key: followUpMessages › appends the assistant turn then all tool results in one user message

tests.description: A paused server tool needs the assistant's partial content echoed back, and nothing else, or the search cannot resume.
tests.key: followUpMessages › echoes the assistant content back to resume a paused turn

tests.description: The seed idea is preserved verbatim through the whole product; the MCP view must not be where it gets paraphrased away.
tests.key: formatMapDetail › includes the title, phase and verbatim seed idea

tests.description: A map created through MCP has no conversation yet; an empty section would read as a truncated response.
tests.key: formatMapDetail › marks an empty conversation explicitly

tests.description: A map whose nodes have all been removed still has to render.
tests.key: formatMapDetail › renders a map with no nodes

tests.description: A client needs both views to reason about the map the way the UI does.
tests.key: formatMapDetail › renders the conversation and the node tree under their own headings

tests.description: Without the id the client cannot open or modify the map it just listed.
tests.key: formatMapList › leads each row with the id in brackets

tests.description: One map per line keeps the response parseable by a client or a person.
tests.key: formatMapList › puts each map on its own line

tests.description: Phase and counts are how a client picks which map is worth opening.
tests.key: formatMapList › reports the phase and the node and message counts

tests.description: A client asking for maps on a fresh install needs a sentence, not a blank response it might read as a failure.
tests.key: formatMapList › says so plainly when there are no maps

tests.description: A finished map still holds every working node; only the four summary kinds belong on this screen.
tests.key: groupSummaryNodes › ignores kinds that do not belong on the summary screen

tests.description: The screen must render its empty hints rather than crash on a map that reached the phase with nothing filled in.
tests.key: groupSummaryNodes › returns four empty buckets for an empty map

tests.description: Next steps are numbered on screen, so their sequence is meaningful — rendering them in insertion order would mislabel the plan.
tests.key: groupSummaryNodes › sorts each bucket by order, not by input position

tests.description: The summary screen has four regions; each must draw from its own kind, or findings land in the wrong card.
tests.key: groupSummaryNodes › splits nodes into the four summary buckets

tests.description: Web search pauses the turn mid-flight; stopping here would silently drop the research the Research phase depends on.

tests.description: The main path when the model is building the map.
tests.key: interpretTurnResponse › collects tool calls and asks the caller to continue

tests.description: Empty or whitespace-only blocks would render as blank bubbles.
tests.key: interpretTurnResponse › discards empty text blocks

tests.description: The API requires one tool_result per tool_use; a missing one fails the next request outright.
tests.key: interpretTurnResponse › emits one tool_result per tool call, keyed by its id

tests.description: stop_details can be absent, and the caller still needs something to show.
tests.key: interpretTurnResponse › falls back to a readable reason when a refusal carries no explanation

tests.description: A response can carry both a sentence and the map changes it describes.
tests.key: interpretTurnResponse › keeps text and tool calls from the same response

tests.description: A safety decline is not an answer; treating it as one would put the refusal text into the map as though it were thinking.
tests.key: interpretTurnResponse › reports a refusal rather than treating it as an answer

tests.description: The ordinary finish: the partner spoke and wants nothing more.
tests.key: interpretTurnResponse › stops on a plain end_turn and keeps the spoken text

tests.description: A round where only the server-side web_search ran reports tool_use but leaves us nothing to answer — continuing would spin the loop forever.
tests.key: interpretTurnResponse › stops when tool_use is reported but no custom tool was called

tests.description: A malformed or empty response must not throw and lose the turn.
tests.key: interpretTurnResponse › survives an empty or malformed content array

tests.description: Depth is what puts a node on the right row; the database stores only parentId, so the tree has to be reconstructed correctly.
tests.key: layoutMap › assigns depth by ancestry

tests.description: Centring is what makes the map look deliberate rather than left-piled; it is the single most visible property of the layout.
tests.key: layoutMap › centres a parent over its children

tests.description: Overlapping pills would make the map unreadable, and long labels are the case most likely to cause it.
tests.key: layoutMap › never overlaps siblings

tests.description: Rows arrive from the database in creation order, so left-to-right position has to come from the stored order instead.
tests.key: layoutMap › orders siblings by their order field, not insertion order

tests.description: A tree reads as a tree only if each generation sits below the last.
tests.key: layoutMap › puts each level on its own row

tests.description: The reported bounds drive the scale-to-fit calculation, so a node outside them would be clipped out of view.
tests.key: layoutMap › reports bounds that contain every node

tests.description: The map panel renders before any node exists, so the empty case must be a clean zero rather than NaN bounds.
tests.key: layoutMap › returns an empty layout for no nodes

tests.description: A malformed parent chain must not hang the render — the map is drawn on every keystroke of the conversation.
tests.key: layoutMap › terminates on a parent cycle instead of hanging

tests.description: A half-written map should still draw; losing nodes silently would be worse than showing an extra root.
tests.key: layoutMap › treats a node whose parent is missing as a root rather than dropping it

tests.description: Node width tracks its label so text stays on two lines at most, but an unbounded label must not stretch the pill into a paragraph.
tests.key: layoutMap › widens a node to fit a longer label, up to a cap

tests.description: A real phase must pass, or the workspace falls back and shows the wrong step as active.
tests.key: map vocabulary guards › accepts every phase in the loop

tests.description: The kinds the map knows how to draw, including the four that only appear on the summary screen.
tests.key: map vocabulary guards › accepts the node kinds the map can draw

tests.description: Status drives the visual treatment, so only these three are meaningful.
tests.key: map vocabulary guards › accepts the three node statuses

tests.description: applyToolCalls drops unknown kinds rather than storing them; this is the check that makes that possible.
tests.key: map vocabulary guards › rejects a node kind the map has no treatment for

tests.description: A typo or a model hallucination must not become the active phase.
tests.key: map vocabulary guards › rejects a phase that is not part of the loop

tests.description: Anything else would fall through to the default treatment silently.
tests.key: map vocabulary guards › rejects an unknown node status

tests.description: Right after the deconstruct turn the map is all questions; the count is what tells the person how much is still unknown.
tests.key: mapCaption › counts open questions while nothing has been answered

tests.description: A map that is only an idea has nothing to report yet, and claiming progress would be the first thing the person notices as false.
tests.key: mapCaption › describes a bare seed when only the idea exists

tests.description: The caption renders before any node exists, so it must not divide by zero or read as though work had happened.
tests.key: mapCaption › describes an empty map as a bare seed too

tests.description: The idea is the map's subject, not one of its findings — counting it would overstate progress by one on every single map.
tests.key: mapCaption › does not count the root idea as an answered node

tests.description: A change the person just made is the most important thing on screen, so it outranks the arithmetic.
tests.key: mapCaption › prefers the just-updated line over the answered/open split

tests.description: After a direction change the reassurance matters more than the counts: the person needs to know their original idea survived.
tests.key: mapCaption › reports that nothing was lost when something was just updated

tests.description: The mid-conversation state the mockups show: some answers in, some still outstanding.
tests.key: mapCaption › reports the answered/open split once both exist

tests.description: "1 open questions" would undercut the care the rest of the copy takes.
tests.key: mapCaption › singularises a lone open question

tests.description: Pro and risk are the only kinds carrying colour; colour used more widely would stop meaning anything.
tests.key: nodeShellClasses › accents risk and pro nodes, and only those

tests.description: Dashed-and-unfilled is how the map says "nobody has answered this" — the provisional look is the whole point.
tests.key: nodeShellClasses › draws an unanswered question dashed and unfilled

tests.description: Most nodes are ordinary settled facts and must render as plain ink pills.
tests.key: nodeShellClasses › falls back to the plain answered treatment for an ordinary kind

tests.description: The root is the map's subject and the only dark shape on the page; losing that fill would leave the map without a visual anchor.
tests.key: nodeShellClasses › fills the root idea solid, the one dark shape on the page

tests.description: Lime marks exactly what just changed, which is what makes a direction change legible at a glance.
tests.key: nodeShellClasses › gives the just-changed node the lime border

tests.description: Gaps are the most valuable finding on the map, not a warning — the mockups draw them as plain pills, and an earlier build wrongly reddened them.
tests.key: nodeShellClasses › leaves a gap node neutral

tests.description: Exactly one thing per screen wears the lime, and it is what just changed — an accent colour must not steal it.
tests.key: nodeShellClasses › lets "updated" win over an accent kind

tests.description: A root that is somehow also "updated" is still the map's subject, so the root treatment has to win.
tests.key: nodeShellClasses › lets the root treatment win over every other rule

tests.description: A research node is what the partner just went and found, so it carries the lime outline and the magnifier.
tests.key: nodeShellClasses › marks a research node as a find

tests.description: A kind the map has no treatment for would render as an untyped blob, so it is dropped rather than stored.
tests.key: planMapMutations › drops a node whose kind the map cannot draw

tests.description: An empty pill is worse than no pill — it takes up map space saying nothing.
tests.key: planMapMutations › drops a node with a blank label

tests.description: An unrecognised status would fall through to the default treatment silently; normalising it makes the fallback explicit.
tests.key: planMapMutations › falls back to answered for an unknown status

tests.description: One turn routinely adds nodes, resolves a question, and moves the phase on.
tests.key: planMapMutations › handles adds, updates and a phase change in one turn

tests.description: An invalid phase must leave the map where it was rather than break the nav.
tests.key: planMapMutations › ignores a phase that is not part of the loop

tests.description: An update naming no real change would be a pointless write.
tests.key: planMapMutations › ignores an update that carries no valid fields

tests.description: Without an id there is nothing to target.
tests.key: planMapMutations › ignores an update with no id

tests.description: "updated" is how the map marks what just changed; it must survive intact.
tests.key: planMapMutations › keeps a valid status

tests.description: A root idea has no parent, and must not invent one.
tests.key: planMapMutations › leaves parentRef null when none is given

tests.description: Sibling position on screen comes from this index.
tests.key: planMapMutations › numbers siblings in the order they arrive

tests.description: The ordinary path: a valid node survives with its fields intact.
tests.key: planMapMutations › plans an insert for a valid node

tests.description: Resolving an answered question is the most common update.
tests.key: planMapMutations › plans an update with only the fields supplied

tests.description: A parent must be written before the child naming it, so the order the model sent has to be preserved exactly.
tests.key: planMapMutations › preserves insert order so parents precede their children

tests.description: The phase drives the nav and the summary-screen switch.
tests.key: planMapMutations › records a valid phase change

tests.description: A turn that only talks changes nothing on the map.
tests.key: planMapMutations › returns an empty plan for no calls

tests.description: A malformed tool call must not throw mid-turn and lose the whole reply.
tests.key: planMapMutations › survives a call with a missing or malformed input

tests.description: Text spoken before a tool call must not be dropped when the loop continues.
tests.key: runTurn › accumulates text across rounds

tests.description: The core loop: a tool round must be answered and the conversation resumed.
tests.key: runTurn › loops after a tool round and collects the calls

tests.description: The map's current state is what lets the model target existing nodes by id.
tests.key: runTurn › passes the map summary to the model as system context

tests.description: Without credentials the route must be able to say so plainly rather than surface a generic 500 from a failed request.
tests.key: runTurn › refuses up front when there are no credentials and no injected client

tests.description: A paused server-side search must be resumed rather than treated as the end.
tests.key: runTurn › resumes a turn paused by a server-side tool

tests.description: A plain reply should cost exactly one request.
tests.key: runTurn › returns the spoken text after a single round

tests.description: The next request must carry the tool results, or the API rejects it.
tests.key: runTurn › sends the tool results back on the following request

tests.description: A model that keeps asking for tools must not spin forever and hang the request; the bound is the only thing standing between that and a hung page.
tests.key: runTurn › stops after the iteration bound when tool calls never end

tests.description: A refusal must reach the caller as an error, not be presented as thinking.
tests.key: runTurn › throws with the refusal explanation

tests.description: Only a line that ENDS in "?" is being asked of the person; a question mark inside a sentence is usually quoting them back to themselves.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › does not treat a mid-line question mark as a question line

tests.description: A model reply often carries blank lines; rendering them would open gaps in the bubble.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › drops blank lines rather than rendering empty paragraphs

tests.description: Ordinary prose must stay ordinary — over-marking would flatten the distinction that makes questions stand out.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › leaves a statement unmarked

tests.description: A question is what the partner is asking of the person, so it must be detected for the panel to give it weight.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › marks a line ending in a question mark as a question

tests.description: An empty reply must render nothing rather than an empty bubble.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › returns nothing for empty or whitespace-only content

tests.description: The real shape of an assistant reply: a lead-in sentence followed by the two or three questions worth asking.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › splits a multi-line reply and marks only the questions

tests.description: Trailing spaces would otherwise defeat the "?" check and lose a question.
tests.key: splitAssistantLines › trims surrounding whitespace on each line

tests.description: Without the id, the model cannot target a node with update_node.
tests.key: summarizeMap › includes each node id in brackets

tests.description: Indentation is how the flat list conveys the tree; without it the model cannot tell a child from a sibling.
tests.key: summarizeMap › indents children beneath their parent

tests.description: Depth must keep increasing so a three-level map does not read as flat.
tests.key: summarizeMap › indents deeper for a grandchild

tests.description: Kind and status tell the model what is settled and what is still open.
tests.key: summarizeMap › names each node kind and status

tests.description: Nodes arrive flat and unordered from the database; every one must appear exactly once regardless of input order.
tests.key: summarizeMap › renders every node exactly once, whatever order they arrive in

tests.description: The model must be told plainly when there is nothing yet, rather than receiving an empty string it might read as a truncation.
tests.key: summarizeMap › says so explicitly when the map is empty

tests.description: The stored role column is a free string; an assistant turn must survive as one or the conversation loses its shape on the next request.
tests.key: toMessageParams › preserves assistant and user turns

tests.description: A brand-new map has no history yet.
tests.key: toMessageParams › returns nothing for an empty history

tests.description: Anything unexpected must land somewhere rather than throw mid-conversation and lose the turn the person just typed.
tests.key: toMessageParams › treats an unrecognised role as a user turn
